articles.title: Caitlin Clark leaves fans speechless as she reveals how she wrapped up one of her busiest months
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark turned a month filled with games and big performances into a post.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark turned a month filled with games and big performances into a post.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark had an August that was difficult to sum up in a single image . The Indiana Fever star went through a month packed with games, important moments and performances that helped keep her team in the fight near the top of the WNBA , but she has now decided to look back and preserve some of those days in a much more personal way.

The basketball star shared an August recap on Instagram featuring different images from what she has experienced over the past few weeks. Some of them were related to basketball, while others captured small details from the days surrounding each game, offering a different look at a month that ended up being especially intense for her .

August had a little bit of everything for Caitlin Clark

Indiana's schedule did not give Clark much room to slow down. During August, the Fever played 11 games, finishing with a 7-4 record during a crucial stretch of the regular season with the Playoffs approaching.

The month began with two consecutive losses against the Minnesota Lynx and Las Vegas Aces , but Indiana quickly responded. The Fever then picked up wins against the Chicago Sky, New York Liberty, Dallas Wings, Atlanta Dream and Toronto Tempo , before suffering another loss to Dallas and another against New York.

The final stretch looked different. Indiana dominated Chicago on August 23 and closed out the month with another convincing victory, this time a 111-91 win over the Connecticut Sun .

And it was in that final game that Clark put the finishing touch on a strong month on the court.

The final game turned into a special night

Against Connecticut, Clark delivered one of her best performances of the month. In 34 minutes, she finished with 34 points, 12 assists, 5 rebounds and 3 steals, while shooting 6-for-12 from three-point range .

The 12 assists carried extra significance, as they pushed her past the 300-assist mark for the season.

But Clark's recap was not limited to what happened during the 40 minutes of each game.

Then came the details Caitlin wanted to keep

Among the images she chose to remember August is an opening photo of Clark holding several pairs of basketball sneakers. The scene feels like a small glimpse into everything that has accompanied her demanding schedule throughout the month .

Other photos show different moments from her days around the games. In one, she wears black Nike sweatpants with white stripes, white sneakers, her hair down and headphones, while another shows her in brown Nike sweatpants , a white hoodie and white sneakers, again with her hair down.

They are simple details, but that is precisely what makes the recap interesting: it is not all about statistics or results. Clark also chose to preserve small scenes from before the games and the moments that make up the routine of such a demanding season.

Among all the images from August, her post ultimately became something of an album capturing what this summer has looked like for her.

A summer that can also be measured in numbers

Beyond the photographs, Clark's current form helps explain why August carried so much weight.

The Indiana guard is averaging 22.5 points and 8.4 assists per game during the 2026 season . After dealing with back discomfort midway through the campaign, she also reached the end of August saying that she was in the best physical condition of her career.

But now, the pace is about to change completely.

The WNBA will enter a break from August 31 through September 16 because of the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Germany .

Clark will join Team USA for the tournament before returning to Indiana for the final games of the regular season. The Fever will be back in action on September 18 against Toronto Tempo, followed by games against the Washington Mystics and Minnesota Lynx before the Playoffs begin .

articles.title: Team USA loses two stars just before the FIBA World Cup: A"ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum will not travel
articles.standfirst: The United States makes its debut this Friday against China with two hugely significant absences at the FIBA World Cup.
articles.summary: The United States makes its debut this Friday against China with two hugely significant absences at the FIBA World Cup.
articles.body:
'A A"ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum will not be able to compete in the tournament due to health issues and are forcing Team USA to alter its plans when the countdown is already underway.'

The United States announced this Monday the withdrawal of both players, who will be replaced by their Washington teammates Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron.

Two absences that change the outlook

The absence of both players shook the start of the women's basketball World Cup.

The absence of A"ja is especially significant. The Las Vegas Aces star, a four-time WNBA MVP , arrived as one of the team's leaders.

With her selection, Wilson was chosen as the standout player of the Paris 2024 Olympic Games and the 2022 World Cup . The United States loses a gem for the meeting of the best national teams in the world.

During the first part of the season, the player had borne a significant workload and needed time to rest

"In Plum's case, she has had a calf injury for a long time, and she has played a large part of the WNBA season with it without recovering 100%. It is also a hard blow for the national team.

The unexpected opportunity for Iriafen and Citron

The story now has two new protagonists. Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron, teammates in Washington , will be responsible for filling the spots left by Wilson and Plum .

Both had previously participated in the national team's camps, but now the situation is completely different: they will have the chance to be part of the team that will try to defend the historic dominance of the United States in the World Cups.

The original Team USA roster had already been announced in early August and was led by names such as Caitlin Clark, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Paige Bueckers, Angel Reese and Wilson herself. Plum was also part of that group of 12 players.

Now, just days before the debut, the United States will have to face the World Cup without two of its most experienced stars. The objective remains the same: to lift the trophy again. But the road to that fifth consecutive title has just become more complicated.

articles.title: Angel Reese avoids suspension after WNBA rescinds controversial eighth technical foul
articles.summary: Angel Reese avoided an automatic one-game suspension after the WNBA rescinded what had initially been ruled her eighth technical foul of the season. The call came after an incident with Portland’s Carla Leite, but the league reversed it shortly after the game. Reese remains at seven technical fouls and will not receive the $1,500 fine or suspension.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark looks back and ranks the defining moments of her WNBA and NCAA career
articles.standfirst: Clark has established many records during her career in Iowa and Indiana
articles.summary: Clark has established many records during her career in Iowa and Indiana
articles.body:
The 30th WNBA season is on a short break until September 17th due to the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, and when the action returns all 15 teams will play the final four remaining games in their schedule during the last week of the regular season, which concludes on September 24 .

These final games will serve to sort out playoff seedings and major individual honors. In the MVP race , the battle has narrowed down to a fierce two-player contest between four-time winner A'ja Wilson , who is a last-minute withdrawal from the World Cup due to health reasons and is leading the league in scoring for a third consecutive year.

The other player is Caitlin Clark , whose unprecedented offensive production accounts for a staggering 41.4 points created per game , standing as the highest mark in league history backed by 22.5 PPG and a league-leading 8.4 APG .

Caitlin Clark Ranks Her Top Career Milestones

With the league on pause, State Farm , one of Caitlin Clark's premier sponsors, produced a feature video asking the superstar guard to rank her defining basketball moments across her legendary NCAA run with Iowa and her professional career with the Indiana Fever , where she has already established numerous all-time records.

Clark noted that every milestone holds a unique place in her journey, but she awarded the top spot to the historic shot against Michigan in 2024 that officially crowned her the NCAA all-time leading scorer , men and women included.

Clark finished her collegiate career in Iowa City with an astonishing 3,951 total points , a standard that looks virtually unbreakable given her career average of nearly 30 points per game.

Taking second place on her personal list was capturing the Rookie of the Year award , punctuated by a historic debut campaign where she set single-season rookie records for points (769) , three-pointers ( 122 ), and assists ( 337 ).

Rounding out the podium at third was the milestone night she secured her first WNBA triple-double , registering 19 points, 12 rebounds, and 13 assists , to become the first rookie in league history and the first Fever player to accomplish the feat in a victory over New York.

From All-Star Highlights to Overcoming Early Rookie Struggles

The fourth entry on Clark's countdown highlighted her appearance in the WNBA All-Star Game against Team USA prior to the Paris Olympic Games.

That showcase stands as the most-watched All-Star Game in league history , and Clark added to the spectacle by setting the rookie single-game assist record with 10 dimes while leading her squad to victory.

Taking the fifth spot was reaching the 1,000 career point threshold during the opening game of this season, a milestone she humbly admitted carried little personal weight at the moment since she wasn't even tracking when it happened.

Finally, rounding out the list at sixth, Clark looked back at her very first professional regular-season game, a tough loss to the Connecticut Sun where she finished with 20 points alongside a WNBA debut-record 10 turnovers .

Now, at just 24 years old and playing the most dominant basketball of her life, Clark is positioned to add plenty of new unforgettable chapters to her resume over the final stretch of this season and for years to come.

articles.title: Enes Kanter calls for WNBA ‘peace summit’ as Caitlyn Jenner agrees to moderate debate
articles.standfirst: The former NBA player's latest challenge is part of a broader campaign he has launched in recent weeks
articles.summary: The former NBA player's latest challenge is part of a broader campaign he has launched in recent weeks
articles.body:
F ormer NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom is escalating his campaign against the WNBA’s transgender eligibility policies, this time with a proposal he says could bring one of sports’ most divisive debates into the open. Kanter has publicly challenged WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert to participate in what he calls a “peace summit,” a public discussion about the league’s eligibility rules.

According to Kanter, Olympic gold medalist and television personality Caitlyn Jenner has already agreed to serve as moderator if the event takes place. The proposal marks the latest chapter in a controversy that has placed the former NBA veteran at the center of a growing conversation about gender eligibility in women's sports.

Kanter takes direct aim at WNBA leadership

In a post on X, Kanter framed the proposed summit as an opportunity for a transparent and respectful discussion rather than another round of private meetings and public statements. “The whole world is laughing at you. You have turned the WNBA into a laughingstock,” Kanter wrote, directing his criticism toward league leadership.

He then called on Engelbert and the league to engage in a public conversation. “Let's have the peace summit. No shouting. No hiding. No carefully scripted statements,” Kanter added. According to Kanter, Jenner is willing to moderate the discussion, which he believes would allow all sides to address questions surrounding the league’s policies in front of a national audience.

“Let's sit across the table from each other, have an open and respectful conversation, and address the questions millions of people are asking,” he wrote. As of Monday, the WNBA had not publicly responded to Kanter's proposal.

A campaign that has drawn national attention

Kanter's latest challenge is part of a broader campaign he has launched in recent weeks. The former Boston Celtics, New York Knicks and Oklahoma City Thunder center first drew headlines when he declared himself eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft . His argument centered on what he claims is a lack of specificity in the league's eligibility language regarding biological sex and transgender participation.

The WNBA's collective bargaining agreement states that players must be women, but Kanter has argued that the policy leaves unanswered questions regarding definitions and eligibility standards. His comments quickly generated reactions across the sports world, with supporters praising his willingness to raise the issue and critics dismissing the effort as a publicity stunt.

The debate intensified further when Kanter attended a game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever wearing a shirt that read: “WOMAN: noun. adult human female.” The appearance ended with Kanter being escorted from Chicago's Wintrust Arena. He was later informed that he was banned from the venue, a development that only increased media attention surrounding his campaign.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark ranks behind one star as the best college player ever according to the future WNBA Rookie of the Year
articles.standfirst: Although she never became a national champion, Caitlin Clark holds several NCAA records
articles.summary: Although she never became a national champion, Caitlin Clark holds several NCAA records
articles.body:
With the WNBA season in a break due to the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, it's a good time to remember that the jump from college basketball to the pros is not easy for everyone, but recent rookies who will represent Team USA in the World Cup like Rhyne Howard , Aliyah Boston , Caitlin Clark , Angel Reese , and Paige Bueckers have exceeded expectations, putting the bar high for newcomers.

This season it's the second overall pick Olivia Miles who has excelled, acting as the engine for the best team in the league while firmly entering MVP conversations alongside A'ja Wilson and Caitlin Clark , with the Rookie of the Year award looking like a total lock for her.

Through 38 games, Miles is averaging 19.7 PPG and 6.0 APG , both leading her squad and ranking inside the top eight across the entire WNBA . She has accumulated a total of 749 points , sitting just 20 points behind Caitlin Clark's all-time rookie record of 769 points , and with four games left to play, it is only a matter of time before she establishes a brand-new rookie scoring standard.

Olivia Miles Places Caitlin Clark Just Behind Breanna Stewart in NCAA History

During her stellar collegiate career split between Notre Dame and TCU , Miles accomplished remarkable feats, including becoming the first freshman in tournament history, men's or women's, to log a triple-double , though she never quite reached the ultimate national championship game.

While she never squared off directly against Caitlin Clark's Iowa squad on the college hardwood, Miles readily acknowledges CC's extraordinary greatness, ultimately ranking her as the second-best player in NCAA history , positioned directly behind legendary icon Breanna Stewart.

In a featured media segment following her draft selection, Miles was prompted to navigate a bracket-style format weighing various historical women’s basketball luminaries, a process that steadily winnowed the field down to a final pairing of Clark and Stewart .

When forced to make the definitive selection, Miles leaned toward Stewart. "See, this is hard," Miles explained. "Caitlin has the scoring, the assists. Stewie has four chips and four MVPs. I’m just gonna have to go Stewie just based off her dominance and winning. "

Weighing Championship Rings Against Historic All-Time Scoring Records

Opting for Stewart is hard to argue against statistically, given that she finished her collegiate run with an astonishing 151-5 overall record , captured four consecutive national championships at UConn, earned the Final Four Most Outstanding Player award four times , and stands alone as the only player in women's college basketball history to secure that honor during every single tournament appearance of her career.

On the other hand, Clark carved out a completely different yet equally immortal legacy, leading the Iowa Hawkeyes to back-to-back National Championship appearances while wrapping up her historic tenure as the NCAA Division I all-time leading scorer across both men's and women's basketball with 3,951 career points .

As a two-time national player of the year , Clark also swept the all-time tournament records for total points, assists, and three-pointers , proving that whether one values Stewart's unmatched hardware or Clark's revolutionary statistical dominance, both guards represent the absolute pinnacle of the collegiate game.

articles.title: Could the connection between Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese become the surprise of the World Cup?
articles.standfirst: For years, they starred in one of the most talked-about rivalries in women's basketball, fueling expectations about what could happen when the two stars meet at the FIBA World Cup.
articles.summary: For years, they starred in one of the most talked-about rivalries in women's basketball, fueling expectations about what could happen when the two stars meet at the FIBA World Cup.
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark and Angel Reese have starred in one of the most followed rivalries in women's basketball in recent years. Today, with the possibility of seeing them together on Team USA, a question arises: What kind of connection can they show when they share the court?

A video released today quickly put both figures in the spotlight, sharing a moment during a game that was recorded earlier but that points to a great partnership for what is to come in Berlin.

“Her connection in Berlin will be different”

articles.standfirst: For the second week in a row and for the fourth time in her career, Reese was named Player of the Week
articles.summary: For the second week in a row and for the fourth time in her career, Reese was named Player of the Week
articles.body:
Since entering the league in 2024 both Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark have rewritten the history books, with Clark setting a new season high in assists ( 337 ) during her rookie campaign, a record that was broken the following year with 357 , alongside recording the most assists in a single game with 19 .

Meanwhile, Reese is thoroughly enjoying her new chapter after being traded to Atlanta this season, where she has shattered the WNBA single-season record for most double-doubles with 29 .

She has also rewritten single-game and single-season rebounding standards that feature hauling down 26 boards in a single contest and accumulating 485 total rebounds , a milestone benchmark she aims to push even higher before the regular season concludes as she chases becoming the first player ever to reach 500 rebounds in a single year .

Angel Reese Matches Caitlin Clark With Elite Weekly Honor

Both of those historic rebounding milestones for Reese occurred last week, prompting the WNBA to award her the Eastern Conference Player of the Week honor for the second consecutive week and the fourth time in her professional career, following a dominant stretch where she averaged 14.0 PPG, 17.7 RPG, and 3.7 APG .

With this latest accolade, Reese joins Caitlin Clark as the only players in the league to capture back-to-back Player of the Week awards this season.

articles.title: Angel Reese closes out a historic summer and an unexpected post steals the spotlight
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream star closed out August with a post featuring some of the moments that defined her past few weeks.
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream star closed out August with a post featuring some of the moments that defined her past few weeks.
articles.body:
Without a doubt, August was a busy month for Angel Reese. The player appeared in 10 games with the Atlanta Dream, eight of which ended in victories , a run that ultimately secured the team a spot in the Playoffs.

Individually, she averaged 17 points, 14.5 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game . Her consistency also earned her consecutive Eastern Conference Player of the Week honors .

And while those numbers would already be enough to stand out, Angel took things to another level.

Three records that changed her August

On August 22, Angel recorded 31 points and 14 rebounds against the Phoenix Mercury , setting a new season-high in scoring. Just two days later came the performance that made history.

Against the Los Angeles Sparks, she grabbed 26 rebounds, the most ever recorded by a player in a single game in WNBA history . That same night, she also broke the record for most rebounds in a single season.

Her final major milestone came on August 30, when she posted 15 points and 11 rebounds against the Minnesota Lynx to record her 29th double-double of the year .

But if anything has become clear, it is that Angel has also turned her social media into a space where she shares some of her biggest moments, and this summer closeout was no exception. The player posted a recap featuring several photos from on and off the court, including one with a young fan posing beside her while Angel holds her own Barbie . Beyond the moment itself, the photo reflects the connection the star has built with her youngest admirers.

A different side of her style

Fashion also had a place in the recap. In one of the photos, Angel wears a red jacket, black pants, a red bag with thick white lines, dark sunglasses and matching shoes . Later, she completely changes the look with light-wash jeans, a black top, a belt, gold jewelry and a black bag.

A photo with Nneka Ogwumike

The collection also includes Nneka Ogwumike, one of the WNBA's most recognized figures. A champion, MVP, 11-time All-Star and president of the WNBPA , Ogwumike shares a moment with Angel as the two pose in a semi-embrace, showing the closeness they have developed within the league.

Their relationship is shaped by admiration and respect, and the photo offers a glimpse of the connections Angel has formed while building her own path in the WNBA.

September already has her next destination

Now, as a new month begins, the calendar enters a different stage. The WNBA will take a break for the international FIBA tournament , meaning Angel will not return to action with Atlanta until September 17.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese have to build a strong duo to adjust to the changes on Team USA
articles.standfirst: Two major absences put more responsibility on the younger core
articles.summary: Two major absences put more responsibility on the younger core
articles.body:
T he U.S. basketball team heading to the World Cup has made two considerable changes to its roster. Now, the younger players will have to build a solid team capable of competing for gold. Team USA enters the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup as the favorite, but the players will have to work together to achieve that goal.

Kelsey Plum and A’ja Wilson have been dropped from the roster for health reasons , paving the way for Mystics guard Sonia Citron and forward Kiki Iriafen. The changes come just days before Team USA tips off the tournament in Berlin, where the players are already preparing for their games.

Team chemistry will be key with two veterans out

Wilson has been dealing with a recurrent back issue over the last week and apparently did not want to exacerbate it. P lum, meanwhile, has been dealing with a calf issue for most of the season and did everything she could to make the World Cup squad, but could not meet the tight timeline.

The current Team USA roster now relies heavily on its young core to get the job done after two more veterans pulled out . The relationships within the roster will have to stand out, and there is plenty of excitement around seeing what the combination o f Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese will look like while playing on the same team.

Clark and Reese now have a chance to turn their rivalry into chemistry

The egos have to stay aside, with the rivalries left for the WNBA . More importantly, the players have to be honest about each other’s strengths so they can stand out as a team . Clark and Reese are known to have had some tension between them, and Caitlin has also recently had issues with Paige Bueckers, but those situations have to stay in the past. The goal now is to maximize what makes each of them some of the best players in the league.

Team USA enters as the heavy favorite to win the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup, with a roster full of generational talent. Even without four-time MVP A’ja Wilson, the U.S. has the best odds of winning the tournament.

Aliyah Boston, Paige Bueckers, Sonia Citron, Caitlin Clark, Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper, Chelsea Gray, Rhyne Howard, Kiki Iriafen, Angel Reese, Breanna Stewart and Jackie Young make up the 12-player roster. It is a strong group despite the late changes.

The U.S. roster is highlighted by athletes with extensive USA Basketball experience, combining for 10 Olympic and five World Cup gold medals. The team also features nine players making their World Cup debuts. Team USA is seeking its fifth consecutive World Cup gold medal and its 12th overall.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham refuses to say when she last went on a date despite having millions of admirers
articles.standfirst: When asked about her last date, Sophie paused and asked a question of her own: What exactly counts as one?
articles.summary: When asked about her last date, Sophie paused and asked a question of her own: What exactly counts as one?
articles.body:
T he question sounded simple: What was the worst first date Sophie Cunningham had ever been on? But before she could offer an awkward or funny dating story, the Indiana Fever guard revealed something far more personal. “People don't come up to me,” she said. “I don't really go on dates.” For a woman followed and admired by millions, it was an unexpectedly vulnerable admission.

The hosts of the Like A Farmer podcast then tried a different approach. When was the last time she had been on a legitimate date? Cunningham paused and asked what exactly counted as one. Dinner? Meeting someone for the first time? She started to form an answer, laughed nervously and then abruptly stopped herself . “I'm not f****** answering this!” she said before joking that she was going to get kicked off the show. “My life is a mystery,” she added, making it clear that this was one part of herself she was not ready to share.

Cunningham has spoken openly about the qualities she wants in a husband

Cunningham also knows what she wants if someone does find the courage to approach her. She has said she would not date a man shorter than her because she wants a partner who can make her “feel smaller.” She prefers what she describes as a more masculine man and considers initiative, honesty and consistency essential.

A man who never texts first, refuses to organize a date, repeatedly makes excuses or acts secretive with his phone would quickly lose her interest. Most importantly, her Christian faith is at the center of her idea of marriage. She wants a husband who will bring her closer to Christ, lead their home and help their future children develop the same relationship with God.

The last relationship Cunningham publicly acknowledged was with former college athlete Jakob Neidig. In 2020 , she posted a photograph of him wearing her jersey and referred to him as her boyfriend, but the public posts eventually stopped and neither revealed why the relationship ended.

More recently, fans have connected her to Grand Canyon University athletic trainer Frank Adams after the two appeared together at basketball games, a bowling alley and other events. Still, neither has confirmed a romance.

Cunningham may share her humor, opinions and basketball life with the world, but when it comes to her heart, she decides exactly where the public line ends.

Why Sophie Cunningham attracts so much attention

Her physical appearance is undeniably part of her appeal . Cunningham's tall athletic figure, blonde hair, striking smile and confident game-day outfits regularly draw praise online, while her appearance in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit issue introduced her to an even larger audience.

But reducing her popularity to beauty would miss what supporters appear to value most. Fans see someone funny, authentic, loyal and completely comfortable being herself. ESPN reported that one of the messages she receives most often is, “In a world of bullies, be a Sophie.” Her teammates have called her a wild card and a fierce competitor whose energy changes practices and games.

She can be playful one moment and ready to defend someone she loves the next.

Sophie is comfortable playing in front of packed arenas, speaking her mind on controversial subjects and confronting anyone who goes after one of her teammates. Dating apparently makes her feel much less certain.

She believes she may project an intimidating presence, and it is not difficult to understand why. She is 6-foot-1, physically strong, successful, outspoken and accustomed to taking control. The same confidence that makes people admire her from afar may also keep some men from simply walking across the room and saying hello. And if introducing themselves already feels intimidating, imagine asking her out.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s historic month gets overlooked as her Fever teammate takes home a major WNBA award
articles.standfirst: In August, Clark averaged 44.7 points from assists and field goals, the highest total in history
articles.summary: In August, Clark averaged 44.7 points from assists and field goals, the highest total in history
articles.body:
The WNBA season is on a short break due to the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin until September 17, and when the action comes back it will be to determine the final standings as the eight teams that will play the playoffs are already qualified (Minnesota Lynx , Golden State Valkyries , Las Vegas Aces , Atlanta Dream , Indiana Fever , New York Liberty , Washington Mystics , and Dallas Wings ).

The other important thing to look at is the awards, and for MVP the four-time winner A'ja Wilson is the heavy favorite after being selected as the player of the month in the Western Conference for the fourth occasion in the four months of the season becoming the only player in WNBA history to sweep all Player of the Month honors in multiple seasons.

Wilson is leading the league in points ( 26.0 PPG ) for a third straight season and in August she averaged 25.0 PPG, 8.8 RPG, and 2.1 BPK with a 7-5 record for the defending champion Las Vegas squad.

Kelsey Mitchell Takes Home Eastern Conference Honors After Record-Breaking Month

The winner of the Eastern Conference was Kelsey Mitchell , who secured the honor for the second time in her career, with last month marking her first.

Kelsey is right behind the leaders in scoring at 25.0 PPG , sits first in three-point percentage at 45.5% , and throughout August posted the 3rd-highest scoring month by any player in WNBA history by averaging a blistering 28.9 PPG, 1.9 RPG, and 3.1 APG .

It was an undeniably historic stretch in which Mitchell extended her streak to 24 consecutive games scoring 20 or more points .

She and teammate Caitlin Clark have the Indiana Fever rewriting the record books as the most prolific offensive unit in WNBA history, averaging a league-high 97.0 PPG while registering a historic 19 games with 100 or more points.

Caitlin Clark's Staggering August Stat Line Overshadowed

While Mitchell is undoubtedly deserving of the accolade, an argument can be made that, much like the previous month, the league could easily have gone with Caitlin Clark .

During August, Clark became the first player to average 24.4 PPG and 9.4 APG in a single month, with her 24.4 points standing as the highest mark ever generated by a guard .

She accounted for or assisted on 44.7 points per game , which sets a new WNBA benchmark for a single month, alongside recording two games with 30+ points and 10+ assists , surpassing any other player in league history.

For the entire 2026 campaign, her unprecedented offensive production accounts for a staggering 41.4 points created per game , the highest mark in league history, complemented by 22.5 PPG (ranking third overall) and a league-leading 8.4 APG .

While she is now fully focused on international duty at the World Cup and thrilled for Mitchell's success, her historic output demands recognition as one of the most remarkable stretches the sport has ever witnessed.

articles.standfirst: Miles needs only 20 more points to become the rookie with the most points in a single season in WNBA history
articles.summary: Miles needs only 20 more points to become the rookie with the most points in a single season in WNBA history
articles.body:
The WNBA is on a break until September 17 due to the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Germany, and when it comes back all teams will play their four remaining games to see how the standings will finish as the eight teams that will be on the playoffs have already qualified.

As it looks it seems the Minnesota Lynx will finish as the top team in the standings a place they have been all season even with their star player Napheesa Collier out for more than half of the season.

But even with Collier out the team has looked amazing especially rookie Olivia Miles who is averaging 19.7 PPG and 6.0 APG , both leading her squad and ranking inside the top eight across the entire WNBA.

Olivia Miles Sweeps Rookie of the Month Honors

Miles was awarded the rookie of the month for August going a perfect 4-for-4 in monthly honors this season. Miles is now tied with seven players who also have 4 WNBA Rookie of the Month awards , a historic list that includes Caitlin Clark (2024), Rhyne Howard (2022), Michaela Onyenwere (2021), Breanna Stewart (2016), Elena Delle Donne (2013), Nneka Ogwumike (2012) and Tina Charles (2010).

Of course, all of these players went on to win Rookie of the Year . Miles has essentially locked up that honor since claiming her first award, which was confirmed when Azzi Fudd was sidelined for the rest of the season.

Her debut campaign is historic because she has accumulated a total of 749 points , sitting just 20 points behind Caitlin Clark's all-time rookie record of 769 points , and with four games left to play, it is only a matter of time before she establishes a brand-new rookie scoring standard.

Looking back at draft night, it is safe to say the Dallas Wings are likely second-guessing passing on her with the first overall pick.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers steals Team USA’s dance video with hilariously awkward twerking attempt
articles.summary: Team USA may be preparing for the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup, but Angel Reese and several of her teammates still found time to have some fun before the competition begins.
articles.body:
Team USA may be preparing for the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup, but Angel Reese and several of her teammates still found time to have some fun before the competition begins.

Wearing their USA jerseys, the players took turns dancing and twerking for the camera. Everything appeared to be going smoothly until Paige Bueckers decided to join in and turned the video into pure comedy.

The Dallas Wings star went upside down against a wall and gave twerking her best shot, but the movement simply wasn’t there. Her awkward attempt looked nothing like those of her teammates, and that was exactly what made it so funny.

Bueckers deserves credit for fully committing to the moment even when it became obvious that twerking might not be one of her many talents. On the basketball court, she can make almost anything look easy. This time, however, her body refused to cooperate.

The lighthearted video offered a glimpse of the chemistry inside Team USA before its World Cup opener against China on September 4.

articles.title: West Wilson comes under fire following Sophie Cunningham's controversial comment about transgender athletes on podcast
articles.standfirst: The Fever guard’s show has gone weeks without a new episode during the biggest controversy of her season
articles.summary: The Fever guard’s show has gone weeks without a new episode during the biggest controversy of her season
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has spent the past several weeks at the center of one of the WNBA ’s loudest off-court debates, yet the podcast built around her outspoken personality has disappeared at exactly the moment many listeners might have expected it to become more active.

Show Me Something, the Indiana Fever guard’s podcast with longtime friend and reality television personality West Wilson , hasn't released a new episode since July 21. That silence has stood out because Cunningham has barely vanished from public view.

She continued to appear on USA Network’s WNBA coverage, remained active on social media and posted sponsored content while discussion of her comments about transgender athletes has spread across television, podcasts and online platforms.

Wilson complicated that conversation further when he publicly disagreed with Cunningham ’s position.

He called transgender women competing in women’s sports a “borderline nonexistent issue” and argued that the subject is amplified in ways that distract from what he described as “actual harmful sh*t,” including rising living costs.

A podcast built on strong opinions

That disagreement was especially notable because Show Me Something had quickly established itself as a place where Cunningham was willing to speak openly about the league.

She used early episodes to discuss officiating, league decisions and the treatment of Fever teammate Caitlin Clark , helping give the show a sharper identity than a traditional athlete interview podcast.

Then the biggest controversy of Cunningham ’s season arrived, and the show went quiet. There has been no public explanation for the hiatus.

The silence has only become more conspicuous because Cunningham has continued fulfilling other media obligations.

Wilson , meanwhile, has also been navigating a separate controversy after his role on Bravo’s Summer House ended amid fallout from a highly publicized romantic situation involving his ex-girlfriend’s best friend.

That would ordinarily give two opinionated podcast hosts plenty to discuss. Instead, listeners have been left waiting.

Cunningham shifts attention back toward family

Cunningham has used the WNBA’s current break during the FIBA Women’s World Cup to step away from some of the noise and spend time with family in Missouri.

She recently shared a lighthearted update about eating locally raised ground chuck, writing: “I just ate ground chuck that one of our family friends raised, and boyyy was it yummy and fresh!”

The break could also help her basketball-wise. Cunningham is averaging 8.3 points this season while shooting 43.4 percent from three, but her numbers have dipped over her last seven games to 5.0 points per game on 31.8 percent shooting from deep.

Indiana sits at 26-14 with six games remaining as it prepares for the postseason. Cunningham has made clear that she would prefer the off-court attention to settle down so she can focus on basketball.

Her podcast has certainly become quieter. The unanswered question is whether that silence is temporary or whether Cunningham and Wilson ’s public disagreement changed the future of Show Me Something altogether.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham is branded a hypocrite after a resurfaced video goes viral
articles.standfirst: A resurfaced video has added another layer to the controversy surrounding Sophie Cunningham
articles.summary: A resurfaced video has added another layer to the controversy surrounding Sophie Cunningham
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has continued to face criticism after making controversial comments about who should not be allowed to play in the WNBA, referring to transgender women. The comments quickly drew backlash from the community, with several WNBA fans labeling Cunningham transphobic. The discussion also moved beyond basketball, opening up a broader national debate.

A resurfaced video is bringing her athletic past into the conversation

The video shows Cunningham playing football on a men’s team, leading fans to call her a hypocrite . Cunningham served as a placekicker for the boys' varsity football team at Rock Bridge High School in Columbia, Missouri.

She stepped in as an injury replacement kicker during her senior year after the team’s regular starting kicker tore his ACL. Cunningham famously made a 45-yard field goal while dealing with a stress fracture in her foot, which required her to wear a walking boot during a related halftime contest. During her brief stint filling in on special teams, Cunningham went 2-for-4 on field goal attempts.

The resurfaced footage has reignited the debate around her comments

This is where some fans have drawn comparisons between Cunningham’s past and her current position. They point to her time on a boys’ football team while now arguing that transgender women should face restrictions based solely on sex in women’s sports.

For those critics, the difference between the two situations has fueled the hypocrisy accusations surrounding her comments. The resurfaced video has now become another point of discussion as the backlash surrounding Cunningham’s comments continues to spread across social media.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom is taking legal action against the Chicago Sky
articles.standfirst: A courtside confrontation turned into a legal battle.
articles.summary: A courtside confrontation turned into a legal battle.
articles.body:
E nes Kanter Freedom has filed a lawsuit against the Chicago Sky and the operators of Wintrust Arena , claiming that his rights protected under the First Amendment were violated after he was removed from a team home game and later banned from attending WNBA games at the venue.

The 15-page lawsuit was filed Thursday in the Northern District of Illinois Eastern Division . In addition to the Chicago Sky, the former NBA player named the City of Chicago and the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, the organization responsible for operating and managing Wintrust Arena, as defendants.

The incident that sparked the dispute occurred on August 23 during the matchup between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever, when Kanter Freedom was involved in a verbal exchange with Sky point guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter.

The former NBA player was sitting courtside wearing a black T-shirt that read:

"WOMAN noun. adult human female."

During a timeout, Cloud approached Kanter Freedom and began confronting him. The former player stood up with his arms extended and took a few steps toward the court, but security intervened before he could move any farther and later instructed him to leave the arena.

Chicago Sky defend Kanter Freedom’s ejection

Sky owner Michael Alter explained that Kanter Freedom began to “chirp” and “engage” with Cloud, who has been a vocal supporter of LGBTQ+ rights .

“[Kanter Freedom] has demonstrated to us, unequivocally, that he has the potential to be a threat. He is not able to control himself to the extent where we can feel comfortable that he may not step toward the court again and toward the players. That is the basis for which we will not permit him into the building until such time as he can prove otherwise,” Alter said last week.

The executive said he respects the First Amendment and people’s right to express their political, religious or personal beliefs. However, he emphasized that fans attending games must follow the rules established by the league and the teams.

“I heard him say, ‘Well, I didn’t cross the baseline,’ as if though that’s some magical threshold,” Alter said. “One reason he didn’t cross the baseline was because he was prevented from doing so. But regardless of that, the security people’s job is not to wait until a threat intensifies. It’s to prevent a threat from happening when a perceived threat occurs, and that’s exactly what they did.”

Alter added that security personnel acted because Kanter Freedom began walking toward the court, and they could not wait to determine how far he would go or what he would do once he got there.

articles.title: Cathy Engelbert out as WNBA boss after Caitlin Clark firestorms and bitter trans athlete battle
articles.standfirst: WNBA chief steps down after years of explosive growth and mounting criticism from players and fans
articles.summary: WNBA chief steps down after years of explosive growth and mounting criticism from players and fans
articles.body:
Cathy Engelbert is set to leave her position as WNBA commissioner at the end of 2026, bringing an end to a seven-year tenure that transformed the league while also exposing deep divisions over its direction.

The WNBA confirmed Friday that Engelbert , 61, will retire after the season. She became the league’s first commissioner in 2019 after previously leading Deloitte, taking charge of a competition with significant potential but far less mainstream attention than it commands today.

Her tenure has delivered major investment, new media agreements and an ambitious expansion plan. The league is scheduled to grow from 12 teams to 18 by 2030, while a new collective bargaining agreement has created the first million-dollar player salaries in WNBA history.

But the remarkable commercial growth has been accompanied by increasingly difficult challenges. Engelbert has faced criticism over player relations, officiating, safety concerns and the league’s handling of controversies involving some of its biggest stars.

Caitlin Clark’s arrival in 2024 became a defining moment. The Indiana Fever guard helped propel the WNBA into a new era of television audiences, attendance and public interest, but the attention surrounding her also generated heated arguments about how the league handled hostile fan behavior, physical play and the treatment of its rising superstar.

Those arguments were only one part of the turbulence surrounding Engelbert’s final seasons.

Engelbert leaves behind a WNBA transformed by growth and controversy

The increasingly divisive debate over transgender athletes has created another major flashpoint. Fever guard Sophie Cunningham attracted widespread attention after speaking about protecting young girls in women’s sports, prompting fierce reactions from supporters and critics.

Demonstrations and counter-protests have subsequently appeared around games, showing how cultural conflicts have increasingly spilled into the league.

Engelbert’s relationship with players has also been tested. Players have previously voiced frustrations about compensation, officiating, communication and trust in the league’s leadership.

Negotiations over the latest collective bargaining agreement were lengthy and tense before both sides eventually reached an agreement.

Despite those disputes, Engelbert can point to substantial accomplishments. During her time in office, the WNBA has experienced significant increases in viewership, attendance, sponsorship revenue, franchise values and investment.

The league has also continued its expansion, welcoming the Golden State Valkyries in 2025 and the Portland Fire and Toronto Tempo in 2026, with Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia planned for later this decade.

Engelbert has maintained that her decision to retire was her own and that she wasn't pushed out by league stakeholders. She has said she initially expected to remain in the position for roughly three and a half years, meaning her seven-plus seasons ultimately lasted far longer than originally planned.

Her departure now leaves NBA commissioner Adam Silver with the task of selecting a successor at a pivotal moment.

The next commissioner will inherit a WNBA that's bigger, wealthier and more influential than ever, but also a league whose players have become increasingly vocal about what they expect from its leadership.

That could make the choice particularly significant. A former player or experienced female basketball executive could offer a perspective rooted in the realities of the league's athletes.

articles.title: ‘Make the WNBA female again’: Enes Kanter Freedom offers to replace Cathy Engelbert as commissioner
articles.standfirst: Kanter Freedom turns his WNBA controversy into an unexpected pitch for league leadership
articles.summary: Kanter Freedom turns his WNBA controversy into an unexpected pitch for league leadership
articles.body:
Enes Kanter Freedom has thrown his name into the WNBA’s commissioner search, offering to replace Cathy Engelbert after she announced that she’ll step down following the 2026 season.

Engelbert , who became the WNBA’s first commissioner in 2019, announced Friday that she’ll leave the position after more than seven years.

Her tenure has overseen a period of substantial growth for the league, with increased attendance, television audiences, commercial interest and expansion plans.

She’ll remain involved during the transition as the league searches for her successor.

Kanter Freedom , meanwhile, sees the leadership change as an opportunity to promote his long-running views on women’s sports. The former NBA center posted a video on social media making his case for the job, accompanying it with the slogan, “MAKE @WNBA FEMALE AGAIN.”

The 34-year-old has become one of the most vocal figures outside the WNBA regarding the debate over transgender athletes competing in women’s sports.

In his video, he argued that the league needs to establish clearer rules surrounding eligibility and said he’d bring “common sense,” “fairness” and, humorously, “a dictionary” if appointed commissioner.

“If the WNBA is unable to define what a woman is, then I, Enes Kanter Freedom, would be more than happy to step in as commissioner and lead this league back to greatness and restore fairness for all women. I’ll bring common sense. I’ll bring fairness. And yes, I’ll bring a dictionary,” said Kanter Freedom .

Kanter’s commissioner pitch follows federal lawsuit

Just one day before putting himself forward as Engelbert’s potential replacement, Kanter Freedom filed a federal lawsuit involving his removal from a WNBA game in Chicago.

The lawsuit, filed Thursday in the Northern District of Illinois, names the Chicago Sky, the city of Chicago and the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, which operates Wintrust Arena.

Kanter Freedom alleges that his constitutional rights were violated when he was removed from the arena during the Sky’s Aug. 23 game against the Indiana Fever.

Kanter Freedom was sitting courtside while wearing a T-shirt that defined a woman as an “adult human female.” During the third quarter, he became involved in a heated exchange with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.

Video from the incident showed Cloud approaching Kanter Freedom while teammates attempted to hold her back. Kanter Freedom was subsequently escorted from the venue by security.

Two days later, the Sky announced that Kanter Freedom was banned from Wintrust Arena. Sky owner Michael Alter said the organization believed the former NBA player could potentially pose a threat to player safety and questioned whether he could control himself around the court.

Kanter Freedom has strongly disputed that characterization. He has described his removal as an infringement of his First Amendment rights and said he’ll continue speaking publicly about women’s sports and free speech.

The former Boston Celtics center has previously gone even further, publicly expressing an interest in playing in the WNBA himself amid the transgender-athlete debate.

His proposal to become commissioner appears to be another extension of that campaign rather than a realistic bid for a major sports executive position.

Still, with Engelbert preparing to leave and the league entering a new era, Kanter Freedom clearly intends to keep himself at the center of the conversation surrounding the WNBA’s future.

articles.standfirst: Clark was named Player of the Game following the 94–61 victory over China
articles.summary: Clark was named Player of the Game following the 94–61 victory over China
articles.body:
The FIBA Women's World Cup in Berlin has officially tipped off with a busy opening matchday featuring 16 countries competing for a spot in the grand final on Sunday, September 13th .

Held every four years, the tournament has been completely dominated by the United States , which has captured gold in every single edition since 1998 , aside from a bronze finish in 2006, making them heavy favorites to secure their fifth consecutive world title .

Right out of the gate on opening day, basketball powerhouses like Spain , France , and the United States established immediate authority by winning their respective contests by 30 or more points.

France secured the largest blowout with a resounding 99-53 victory over Hungary, while Team USA cruised past China 94-61, propelled by a stellar performance from Caitlin Clark , who electrified the floor off the bench to earn Player of the Game honors.

Caitlin Clark Historic Opening Night Performance

Despite not cracking the starting lineup, Clark dominated the hardwood by logging a team-high 25 minutes , dropping a game-best 14 points (tied with Paige Bueckers ), and dishing out 11 assists .

Clark's inaugural World Cup appearance etched her name into the tournament record books because her 11 dimes not only set a new Team USA single-game record for a player making their debut, but she also became the first player in event history to record 10+ assists with zero turnovers .

Furthermore, she achieved a milestone no American player had touched in nearly three decades, becoming the first representative from the USA to rack up at least 10 assists in a World Cup game since current South Carolina head coach Dawn Staley handed out 12 assists during the gold-medal final against Russia back in 1998.

Staley eventually finished that 1998 tournament with a U.S. record 52 total assists , and if Team USA marches all the way to the final and Clark maintains her blistering distribution pace, she has a legitimate shot at threatening that long-standing benchmark.

Looking ahead, the road continues this Sunday when Team USA squares off against Italy , a squad fresh off defeating Czechia in their opening fixture. Following the Italian matchup, the Americans will wrap up Group D play on Monday against Czechia .

Securing victories in both contests will punch Team USA's ticket straight into the quarterfinals, though finishing second or third in the group stage would force them into an additional qualification playoff match before reaching the final eight.

For much of the past two years, Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese have been defined by rivalry. From their unforgettable NCAA championship clash to countless WNBA battles, the two stars have become central figures in the growth of women’s basketball. Every interaction between them is scrutinized, every matchup generates headlines, and every on-court exchange seems to spark debate among fans.

But Team USA’s opening game at the 2026 FIBA Women’s World Cup offered a reminder that things can look very different when the two stars are wearing the same jersey. Ahead of the Americans’ tournament-opening victory over China in Berlin, Clark and Reese were spotted sharing a brief but amusing moment while checking into the scorer’s table.

As both players prepared to enter the game, Clark appeared eager to get onto the court and moved toward the floor before the substitution process had officially been completed. That prompted Reese to step in with a quick reminder.

Reese told Clark to wait for the buzzer before checking into the game, drawing smiles from nearby teammates and creating a lighthearted moment between two players who have spent much of their careers competing against one another. It was a small interaction, but one that highlighted the chemistry Team USA hopes to build as it pursues a fifth consecutive FIBA Women’s World Cup title.

The Americans certainly looked connected once the game began

Clark helped orchestrate the offense in a dominant 94-61 victory over China, finishing with a 14-point, 11-assist double-double. The Indiana Fever star controlled the pace from the opening quarter and repeatedly found teammates in scoring positions as Team USA showcased the depth that makes it the favorite to win gold.

“Anybody I pass the ball to, it feels like they’re never going to miss a shot,” Clark said after the game. “That’s one of my goals when I come into the game, facilitate, play fast, set up my teammates.” Clark's performance was a perfect example of that approach. She closed the first quarter with an impressive three-point play after weaving through defenders and followed it with a quick three-pointer early in the second quarter.

While Clark directed the offense, Team USA received contributions from throughout the roster. Rhyne Howard and Jackie Young provided scoring punch, while Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier controlled the glass. Paige Bueckers came alive in the second half, scoring 14 points and helping the Americans pull away. By the end of the night, Team USA h ad accumulated 26 assists, nine steals, and six blocks in a performance that underscored its championship aspirations.

Coach was pleased with the balance displayed by her team

Head coach Kara Lawson was particularly pleased with the balance displayed by her team. “We just had a lot of people in a lot of different moments step up and that’s what we need,” Lawson said. “We’re at our best when we have a lot of different people contributing.”

That philosophy could be especially important when it comes to integrating stars such as Clark and Reese. For years, basketball fans have framed the pair as opponents. Their contrasting styles, personalities, and fan bases have fueled one of the sport’s most compelling rivalries. Yet Team USA presents a different challenge: finding ways for elite players to complement one another rather than compete for the spotlight.

The early signs have been encouraging. The brief scorer’s-table exchange may not have altered the outcome of the game, but it offered a glimpse of teammates working together rather than rivals working against each other. Reese’s reminder for Clark t o wait for the buzzer was hardly dramatic, yet it reflected the type of communication and trust that championship teams require.
